ai.description: *Ichthyophis nokrekensis* is a slender caecilian reaching 20–25 cm. It is dark violet-brown with a distinct yellow lateral stripe and a pale snout, distinguished by its 280–300 primary annuli.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ichthyophis nokrekensis* is uniquely distinguished by its distinct, broad, and continuous yellow lateral stripe that extends from the head to the tip of the tail.
ai.habitat: *Ichthyophis nokrekensis* inhabits moist, subtropical broadleaf forests in the Garo Hills, typically found in damp soil near streams at altitudes of 600–900 meters.
ai.behavior: *Ichthyophis nokrekensis* is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows at night to forage for earthworms and small invertebrates in moist soil.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ichthyophis nokrekensis* is oviparous, laying clutches of approximately 20–30 eggs in burrows near water. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically June–July.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ichthyophis nokrekensis* is endemic to the Nokrek Biosphere Reserve in the Garo Hills of Meghalaya, India, occurring at elevations between 400 and 1,100 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Ichthyophis nokrekensis* consists of short, high-pitched, metallic chirps emitted in rapid, rhythmic pulses from within moist, subterranean burrows.
